heroHeadline: US EXPLORES NUCLEAR SHARING EXPANSION TO POLAND & BALTICS (FT/DEFENSE NEWS); ARTICLE 4 CONSULTATION ONGOING ON CONFIRMED RUSSIAN GERAN-2 STRIKE; FORMAL NATO WITHDRAWAL PLAN EXPECTED THIS MONTH; ANKARA SUMMIT 35 DAYS OUT
heroSubtitle: As of June 2, 2026, the Financial Times and Defense News report that the United States is conducting internal NATO discussions about expanding nuclear sharing — deploying B61 dual-capable aircraft to Poland and the Baltic states for the first time in alliance history. No agreement has been reached, but the discussions mark a significant structural development: even as the US reduces conventional contributions to NATO (zero submarines, zero drones, fighter jets cut by one-third, strategic bombers halved per the May 26 Der Spiegel disclosure), nuclear engagement on the eastern flank is potentially expanding. Poland is simultaneously pursuing French bilateral nuclear deterrence as a hedge. Russia's unannounced nuclear exercises in May 2026, combined with the confirmed Russian Geran-2 drone strike on NATO territory at Galati, Romania (forensically confirmed June 1 with Cyrillic stencil 'ГЕРАНЬ-2'), are the immediate drivers. Romania and NATO are formally discussing Article 4 consultation — a formal North Atlantic Council meeting on threats to territorial integrity — without invoking Article 5 collective defense. The US is expected to submit a formal NATO European force-level withdrawal plan to allies as early as this month, formally codifying the 10,200+ troop cuts and hardware reductions ahead of the Ankara Leaders' Summit (July 7–8, 35 days away). The emerging US posture — nuclear sharing potentially expanding eastward to Poland and the Baltics while conventional forces withdraw from western Europe — represents a fundamental reconfiguration of the alliance's deterrence architecture that the Ankara summit must address.
